```ts
// packages/AI/PredictiveStudio/Engine/src/migration/legacy-pipeline-migration.ts
/**
 * @module migration/legacy-pipeline-migration
 * Gives a pipeline its version-1 Prediction Unit and Evaluation Protocol from its legacy columns, archives
 * it, or holds it — each with the reason recorded in the report and on the pipeline. Idempotent:
 * a pipeline already bound to both is skipped. Used by the Action, by the Pipeline Builder for the pipelines it
 * creates, by the truth-suite harness and by the release step.
 */
import { RunView, type IMetadataProvider, type UserInfo } from '@memberjunction/core';
import type { MJEvaluationProtocolEntity, MJMLModelEntity, MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, MJPredictionUnitEntity } from '@memberjunction/core-entities';
import { EscapeSQLString, UUIDsEqual } from '@memberjunction/global';
import {
  ProtocolRows, EvaluationProtocolRules, LegacyPipelines,
  PredictionUnit,
  type Actor, type PredictionUnitSpec,
} from '@memberjunction/predictive-studio-core';
import { RunViewDataAccess } from '../feature-assembly/data-access';
import { CompleteReader } from '../feature-assembly/read-policy';
import { ProviderAssemblyMetadata } from '../feature-assembly/assembly-metadata';
import { RunViewPredictionUnitStore } from '../prediction-unit/unit-store';
import { PredictionUnitVersioning } from '../prediction-unit/unit-versioning';
import type { IEntityFactory } from '../training/types';

export const MIGRATION_ACTOR: Actor = { kind: 'system', component: 'pipeline-migration' };

export interface MigrationReportRow {
  readonly PipelineID: string;
  readonly PipelineName: string;
  readonly Action: 'migrated' | 'would-migrate' | 'archived' | 'would-archive' | 'held' | 'would-hold' | 'skipped' | 'failed';
  readonly Reason: string | null;
  readonly PredictionUnitID: string | null;
  readonly EvaluationProtocolID: string | null;
  /** The date-carved cutoff; null for a seeded-random holdout and for rows that were not migrated. */
  readonly Cutoff: string | null;
  readonly Notes: readonly string[];
}

export interface MigrationDeps {
  readonly Provider: IMetadataProvider;
  readonly User: UserInfo;
  readonly EntityFactory: IEntityFactory;
  /** UTC day of the migration (yyyy-mm-dd); injected for deterministic tests. */
  readonly Today: string;
}

/** One run over the pipelines: the per-pipeline rows and their counts (the Action's outputs). */
export interface MigrationRun {
  readonly Report: readonly MigrationReportRow[];
  readonly MigratedCount: number;
  readonly ArchivedCount: number;
  readonly HeldCount: number;
  readonly SkippedCount: number;
  readonly FailedCount: number;
}

type ReportBase = Omit<MigrationReportRow, 'Action' | 'Reason'>;

/** The unit a pipeline trains under after step 1, with the date column its protocol carves on. */
interface ResolvedUnit {
  readonly Unit: PredictionUnitSpec | null;   // null in a dry run that would create version 1
  readonly DateColumn: string | null;
  readonly Notes: readonly string[];
}

/** The legacy-pipeline data migration (static members on one owner, coding standards §2). */
export class PipelineMigration {
  /** One pipeline: migrate, archive or hold it, with the reason; skipped when archived or already bound to both. */
  public static async EnsurePipelineUnitAndProtocol(p: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, deps: MigrationDeps, dryRun: boolean): Promise<MigrationReportRow> {
    const base: ReportBase = { PipelineID: p.ID, PipelineName: p.Name, PredictionUnitID: p.PredictionUnitID, EvaluationProtocolID: p.EvaluationProtocolID, Cutoff: null, Notes: [] };
    if (p.Status === 'Archived') return { ...base, Action: 'skipped', Reason: 'archived' };
    if (p.PredictionUnitID !== null && p.EvaluationProtocolID !== null) return { ...base, Action: 'skipped', Reason: 'already-migrated' };
    const metadata = new ProviderAssemblyMetadata(deps.Provider);
    const entity = metadata.Entity(p.TargetEntity);
    if (entity === null) return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `target entity "${p.TargetEntity}" is not registered or has a composite key` };

    // 1. The unit: the pipeline's own, or a new version 1 from its legacy columns and declared outcome semantics.
    const resolved = await PipelineMigration.resolveUnit(p, entity, metadata, deps, dryRun, base);
    if ('Action' in resolved) return resolved;
    const notes = [...resolved.Notes];

    // 2. The protocol, from ValidationStrategy / LeakageGuard (over the rows' dates when the unit has a date column).
    const dates = resolved.DateColumn === null ? [] : await PipelineMigration.readColumn(entity.Name, entity.PrimaryKey, resolved.DateColumn, deps);
    const proto = LegacyPipelines.LegacyProtocolInputs(p.ValidationStrategy, p.LeakageGuard, resolved.DateColumn, dates);
    if (proto.Kind === 'archive') return PipelineMigration.archive(p, proto.Reason, deps, dryRun, base);
    notes.push(...proto.Notes);
    const cutoff = proto.Holdout.kind === 'date-carved' ? proto.Holdout.cutoff : null;
    if (dryRun || resolved.Unit === null) return { ...base, Action: 'would-migrate', Reason: null, Cutoff: cutoff, Notes: notes };
    return PipelineMigration.bindProtocol(p, resolved.Unit, proto, deps, { ...base, Cutoff: cutoff, Notes: notes });
  }

  /**
   * Every pipeline (or the listed ones) through `EnsurePipelineUnitAndProtocol`; the Action and the release step call
   * this. Sequential on purpose: each pipeline's rows are validated by the server entities as they save, and the
   * report keeps the pipelines' name order.
   */
  public static async MigratePipelines(deps: MigrationDeps, dryRun: boolean, onlyIds: readonly string[]): Promise<MigrationRun> {
    const pipelines = await RunView.FromMetadataProvider(deps.Provider).RunView<MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity>(
      { EntityName: 'MJ: ML Training Pipelines', OrderBy: 'Name', ResultType: 'entity_object' }, deps.User);
    if (!pipelines.Success) throw new Error(`Loading pipelines failed: ${pipelines.ErrorMessage}`);
    const report: MigrationReportRow[] = [];
    for (const p of pipelines.Results) {
      if (onlyIds.length > 0 && !onlyIds.some((id) => UUIDsEqual(id, p.ID))) continue;
      try {
        report.push(await PipelineMigration.EnsurePipelineUnitAndProtocol(p, deps, dryRun));
      } catch (e) {
        report.push({ PipelineID: p.ID, PipelineName: p.Name, Action: 'failed', Reason: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e), PredictionUnitID: p.PredictionUnitID, EvaluationProtocolID: p.EvaluationProtocolID, Cutoff: null, Notes: [] });
      }
    }
    const count = (...actions: MigrationReportRow['Action'][]): number => report.filter((r) => actions.includes(r.Action)).length;
    return {
      Report: report,
      MigratedCount: count('migrated', 'would-migrate'),
      ArchivedCount: count('archived', 'would-archive'),
      HeldCount: count('held', 'would-hold'),
      SkippedCount: count('skipped'),
      FailedCount: count('failed'),
    };
  }

  /** Step 1: the pipeline's bound unit, or version 1 built from its legacy columns (archive / hold / failed rows end the pipeline). */
  private static async resolveUnit(
    p: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, entity: { readonly Name: string; readonly PrimaryKey: string }, metadata: ProviderAssemblyMetadata,
    deps: MigrationDeps, dryRun: boolean, base: ReportBase,
  ): Promise<ResolvedUnit | MigrationReportRow> {
    if (p.PredictionUnitID !== null) {
      const loaded = await PipelineMigration.loadUnit(p.PredictionUnitID, deps);
      if (loaded === null) return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `Prediction Unit ${p.PredictionUnitID} not found or unreadable` };
      const dateColumn = loaded.rows.kind === 'grain' && loaded.rows.decisionDate.kind === 'column' ? loaded.rows.decisionDate.column : null;
      return { Unit: loaded, DateColumn: dateColumn, Notes: [] };
    }
    const [labels, lineage] = await Promise.all([
      PipelineMigration.readColumn(entity.Name, entity.PrimaryKey, p.TargetVariable, deps),
      PipelineMigration.newestModelLineage(p.ID, deps),
    ]);
    const outcome = LegacyPipelines.LegacyOutcomeCandidates({
      FeatureSteps: p.FeatureSteps, Hyperparameters: p.Hyperparameters, ModelLineage: lineage, TargetVariable: p.TargetVariable, ProblemType: p.ProblemType,
    });
    const mapped = LegacyPipelines.LegacyUnitInputs(p, labels, deps.Today, outcome);
    if (mapped.Kind === 'archive') return PipelineMigration.archive(p, mapped.Reason, deps, dryRun, base);
    if (mapped.Kind === 'hold') return PipelineMigration.hold(p, mapped.Reason, deps, dryRun, base);
    if (dryRun) return { Unit: null, DateColumn: mapped.DateColumn, Notes: mapped.Notes };
    const row = await PredictionUnitVersioning.CreatePredictionUnitV1(mapped.Draft, MIGRATION_ACTOR, deps.EntityFactory, deps.User);
    const parsed = PredictionUnit.ParsePredictionUnitRow(row);
    if (!parsed.Ok) return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `migrated unit does not parse: ${parsed.Errors.join('; ')}`, Notes: mapped.Notes };
    RunViewPredictionUnitStore.ApplyUnitToPipeline(p, row.ID, parsed.Value, metadata);
    return { Unit: parsed.Value, DateColumn: mapped.DateColumn, Notes: mapped.Notes };
  }

  /** Step 3: saves protocol version 1 from the legacy inputs and binds it (with the unit set in step 1) on the pipeline. */
  private static async bindProtocol(
    p: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, unit: PredictionUnitSpec, proto: Extract<ReturnType<typeof LegacyPipelines.LegacyProtocolInputs>, { readonly Kind: 'protocol' }>,
    deps: MigrationDeps, base: ReportBase,
  ): Promise<MigrationReportRow> {
    const draft = EvaluationProtocolRules.DefaultEvaluationProtocolDraft({ Unit: unit, Holdout: proto.Holdout, Candidates: 1, Seed: 42, Name: `${p.Name} — migrated protocol` });
    const withLegacy = { ...draft, exclusions: proto.Exclusions, ...(proto.InnerValidation === null ? {} : { innerValidation: proto.InnerValidation }) };
    const protocolRow = await deps.EntityFactory.getEntityObject<MJEvaluationProtocolEntity>('MJ: Evaluation Protocols', deps.User);
    const id = ProtocolRows.NewVersionRowID();
    ProtocolRows.ApplyProtocolDraftToRow(protocolRow, withLegacy, { ID: id, LineageRootID: id, Version: 1, AuthoredBy: MIGRATION_ACTOR, Description: `Migrated from pipeline "${p.Name}" on ${deps.Today}.` });
    if (!(await protocolRow.Save())) {
      return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `protocol: ${protocolRow.LatestResult?.CompleteMessage || 'save failed'}`, PredictionUnitID: p.PredictionUnitID };
    }
    p.EvaluationProtocolID = protocolRow.ID;
    if (!(await p.Save())) {
      return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `pipeline: ${p.LatestResult?.CompleteMessage || 'save failed'}`, PredictionUnitID: p.PredictionUnitID, EvaluationProtocolID: protocolRow.ID };
    }
    return { ...base, Action: 'migrated', Reason: null, PredictionUnitID: p.PredictionUnitID, EvaluationProtocolID: protocolRow.ID };
  }

  private static async archive(p: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, reason: string, deps: MigrationDeps, dryRun: boolean, base: ReportBase): Promise<MigrationReportRow> {
    if (dryRun) return { ...base, Action: 'would-archive', Reason: reason };
    p.Status = 'Archived';
    p.Description = `${p.Description ? `${p.Description}\n` : ''}Archived by the Prediction Unit migration on ${deps.Today}: ${reason}.`;
    if (!(await p.Save())) return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `archive: ${p.LatestResult?.CompleteMessage || 'save failed'}` };
    return { ...base, Action: 'archived', Reason: reason };
  }

  /** Held: Status unchanged, published models keep scoring, training refused (`unit-required`) until a later run migrates it. */
  private static async hold(p: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, reason: string, deps: MigrationDeps, dryRun: boolean, base: ReportBase): Promise<MigrationReportRow> {
    if (dryRun) return { ...base, Action: 'would-hold', Reason: reason };
    const marker = `Held by the Prediction Unit migration: ${reason}.`;
    if (!(p.Description || '').includes(marker)) {
      p.Description = `${p.Description ? `${p.Description}\n` : ''}${marker} (${deps.Today})`;
      if (!(await p.Save())) return { ...base, Action: 'failed', Reason: `hold: ${p.LatestResult?.CompleteMessage || 'save failed'}` };
    }
    return { ...base, Action: 'held', Reason: reason };
  }

  /** `Lineage` of the pipeline's newest Published model, else its newest model; null when it has none. */
  private static async newestModelLineage(pipelineId: string, deps: MigrationDeps): Promise<string | null> {
    const rv = RunView.FromMetadataProvider(deps.Provider);
    const id = EscapeSQLString(pipelineId);
    for (const filter of [`PipelineID='${id}' AND Status='Published'`, `PipelineID='${id}'`]) {   // the second read only when the first finds nothing
      const r = await rv.RunView<Pick<MJMLModelEntity, 'Lineage'>>(
        { EntityName: 'MJ: ML Models', ExtraFilter: filter, OrderBy: '__mj_CreatedAt DESC', MaxRows: 1, Fields: ['Lineage'], ResultType: 'simple' }, deps.User);
      if (!r.Success) throw new Error(`Loading the models of pipeline ${pipelineId} failed: ${r.ErrorMessage}`);
      const row = r.Results[0];
      if (row !== undefined) return row.Lineage;
    }
    return null;
  }

  /** One column of every row, read completely (a truncated read throws: the mapping must see every row). */
  private static async readColumn(entityName: string, keyField: string, field: string, deps: MigrationDeps): Promise<string[]> {
    const read = await CompleteReader.ReadCompletely(new RunViewDataAccess(deps.User, deps.Provider), { EntityName: entityName, KeyField: keyField, Fields: [field] }, { mode: 'paged', pageSize: 50_000 });
    if (read.Status === 'refused') throw new Error(`Reading ${entityName}.${field} was truncated: ${JSON.stringify(read.Refusal)}`);
    return read.Rows.flatMap((r) => {
      const v = r[field];
      if (v === null || v === undefined) return [];
      return [v instanceof Date ? v.toISOString() : String(v)];
    });
  }

  /** The bound unit version, parsed; null when the row is missing or does not parse (a failed read throws). */
  private static async loadUnit(unitId: string, deps: MigrationDeps): Promise<PredictionUnitSpec | null> {
    const r = await RunView.FromMetadataProvider(deps.Provider).RunView<MJPredictionUnitEntity>(
      { EntityName: 'MJ: Prediction Units', ExtraFilter: `ID='${EscapeSQLString(unitId)}'`, ResultType: 'entity_object' }, deps.User);
    if (!r.Success) throw new Error(`Loading Prediction Unit ${unitId} failed: ${r.ErrorMessage}`);
    const row = r.Results[0];
    if (row === undefined) return null;
    const parsed = PredictionUnit.ParsePredictionUnitRow(row);
    return parsed.Ok ? parsed.Value : null;
  }
}
```

```ts
// packages/AI/PredictiveStudio/Engine/src/actions/migrate-pipelines.action.ts
import type { ActionResultSimple, RunActionParams } from '@memberjunction/actions-base';
import { RegisterClass } from '@memberjunction/global';
import { LogError } from '@memberjunction/core';
import { BaseAction } from '@memberjunction/actions';
import { PipelineMigration } from '../migration/legacy-pipeline-migration';
import { BasePredictiveStudioAction } from './base-predictive-studio.action';

export const MIGRATE_PIPELINES_DRIVER_CLASS = 'PredictiveStudioMigratePipelinesAction';

/** Data migration: every pipeline gets a Prediction Unit and an Evaluation Protocol, is archived, or is held — with the reason. */
@RegisterClass(BaseAction, MIGRATE_PIPELINES_DRIVER_CLASS)
export class PredictiveStudioMigratePipelinesAction extends BasePredictiveStudioAction {
  protected async InternalRunAction(params: RunActionParams): Promise<ActionResultSimple> {
    try {
      const dryRun = this.getBooleanParam(params, 'DryRun') ?? true;   // `??`: an explicit false is a real run
      const deps = { Provider: this.ProviderToUse, User: params.ContextUser, EntityFactory: this.entityFactory(), Today: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10) };
      const run = await PipelineMigration.MigratePipelines(deps, dryRun, this.getStringArrayParam(params, 'PipelineIDs'));
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'Report', JSON.stringify(run.Report));
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'MigratedCount', run.MigratedCount);
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'ArchivedCount', run.ArchivedCount);
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'HeldCount', run.HeldCount);
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'SkippedCount', run.SkippedCount);
      this.addOutputParam(params, 'FailedCount', run.FailedCount);
      const failed = run.Report.filter((r) => r.Action === 'failed');
      return failed.length === 0
        ? this.ok(params, `${dryRun ? 'Dry run: ' : ''}${run.Report.length} pipelines examined.`)
        : this.fail('PARTIAL_FAILURE', `${failed.length} pipelines failed: ${failed.map((f) => `${f.PipelineName}: ${f.Reason ?? ''}`).join('; ')}`);
    } catch (e) {
      LogError(e);
      return this.fail('MIGRATION_FAILED', e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
    }
  }
}
```

  **The advancing decision date (D3-43).** Create `Engine/src/prediction-unit/decision-date-advance.ts` and export it
  from `prediction-unit/index.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * @module prediction-unit/decision-date-advance
 * A fixed decision date with `advance: 'each-run'` (migrated legacy pipelines without an as-of) moves to each
 * run's UTC day: before the run, the engine saves the next unit version with that day and the censoring cutoff moved
 * by the same window, and points the pipeline at it. The model then references the exact version it was trained under.
 */
import type { UserInfo } from '@memberjunction/core';
import type { MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity } from '@memberjunction/core-entities';
import { UUIDsEqual } from '@memberjunction/global';
import { PredictionUnit, type Actor, type PredictionUnitSpec } from '@memberjunction/predictive-studio-core';
import type { IAssemblyMetadata } from '../feature-assembly/assembly-metadata';
import type { IEntityFactory } from '../training/types';
import { UtcDay } from './utc-day';
import { RunViewPredictionUnitStore, type IPredictionUnitStore } from './unit-store';
import { PredictionUnitVersioning, type PredictionUnitDraft } from './unit-versioning';

export const DECISION_DATE_ADVANCE_ACTOR: Actor = { kind: 'system', component: 'decision-date-advance' };

/** Advancing fixed decision dates (static members on one owner, coding standards §2). */
export class DecisionDateAdvance {
  /** Pure: the changes that move an advancing fixed decision date to `runDay`; null when the rule does not advance or is already there. */
  public static DecisionDateAdvanceChanges(unit: PredictionUnitSpec, runDay: string): Partial<PredictionUnitDraft> | null {
    if (unit.rows.kind !== 'grain') return null;
    const rule = unit.rows.decisionDate;
    if (rule.kind !== 'fixed' || rule.advance !== 'each-run' || rule.date === runDay) return null;
    const day = UtcDay.ToUtcDay(runDay);
    if (day === null) throw new Error(`run day ${runDay} is not yyyy-mm-dd`);
    return {
      UnitRows: { ...unit.rows, decisionDate: { kind: 'fixed', date: runDay, advance: 'each-run' } },
      Censoring: { rule: 'exclude-unresolved', cutoff: { kind: 'fixed', at: UtcDay.UtcDayIso(UtcDay.AddUtcDays(day, unit.label.windowDays + unit.label.gapDays)) } },
    };
  }

  /**
   * Advances the pipeline's bound unit when due and returns the unit id to train under. Only the newest version of a
   * lineage advances: a pipeline bound to an older version keeps it (that binding is deliberate). A missing or
   * unparsable unit is left to the engine's own refusal (`loadUnitSpec`).
   */
  public static async AdvanceFixedDecisionDate(
    pipeline: MJMLTrainingPipelineEntity, store: IPredictionUnitStore, runDay: string, metadata: IAssemblyMetadata,
    entityFactory: IEntityFactory, contextUser?: UserInfo,
  ): Promise<string | null> {
    const unitId = pipeline.PredictionUnitID;
    if (unitId === null) return null;
    const row = await store.Load(unitId);
    if (row === null) return unitId;
    const parsed = PredictionUnit.ParsePredictionUnitRow(row);
    if (!parsed.Ok) return unitId;
    const changes = DecisionDateAdvance.DecisionDateAdvanceChanges(parsed.Value, runDay);
    if (changes === null) return unitId;
    const latest = await store.LatestVersion(row.LineageRootID);
    if (latest === null || !UUIDsEqual(latest.ID, row.ID)) return unitId;
    const next = await PredictionUnitVersioning.CreateNextPredictionUnitVersion(row, changes, DECISION_DATE_ADVANCE_ACTOR, entityFactory, contextUser);
    const nextSpec = PredictionUnit.ParsePredictionUnitRow(next);
    if (!nextSpec.Ok) throw new Error(`Advanced unit ${next.ID} does not parse: ${nextSpec.Errors.join('; ')}`);
    RunViewPredictionUnitStore.ApplyUnitToPipeline(pipeline, next.ID, nextSpec.Value, metadata);
    if (!(await pipeline.Save())) throw new Error(`Binding pipeline ${pipeline.ID} to unit ${next.ID} failed: ${pipeline.LatestResult?.CompleteMessage || 'save failed'}`);
    return next.ID;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import type { DecisionDateRule, PredictionUnitSpec } from '@memberjunction/predictive-studio-core';
import { DecisionDateAdvance } from '../decision-date-advance';

const unit = (decisionDate: DecisionDateRule): PredictionUnitSpec => ({

  censoring: { rule: 'exclude-unresolved', cutoff: { kind: 'fixed', at: '2026-10-21' } },

  decision: { action: 'review', actorRole: 'analyst', capacityPerPeriod: null, period: 'month' },
  incumbent: { kind: 'none' }, authoredBy: { kind: 'system', component: 'pipeline-migration' },
});

describe('DecisionDateAdvanceChanges', () => {

      Censoring: { rule: 'exclude-unresolved', cutoff: { kind: 'fixed', at: '2026-11-03' } },
    });
  });
  it('leaves a date already on the run day, a non-advancing fixed date and a column date alone', () => {
    expect(DecisionDateAdvance.DecisionDateAdvanceChanges(unit({ kind: 'fixed', date: '2026-11-02', advance: 'each-run' }), '2026-11-02')).toBeNull();
    expect(DecisionDateAdvance.DecisionDateAdvanceChanges(unit({ kind: 'fixed', date: '2020-01-01' }), '2026-11-02')).toBeNull();
    expect(DecisionDateAdvance.DecisionDateAdvanceChanges(unit({ kind: 'column', column: 'StartDate' }), '2026-11-02')).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```ts
// metadata/remote-operations/types/predictive-studio-train-model.output.ts — whole interface
/** Output of `PredictiveStudio.TrainModel` — the stored gate decision of the run, plus the produced model when the gate did not end in no-signal. */
export interface PredictiveStudioTrainModelOutput {
    /** Id of the produced (Draft) `MJ: ML Models` row; absent when the gate stored no-signal (no model is created). */
    modelId?: string;
    /** Id of the `MJ: ML Training Runs` row recording this attempt. */
    trainingRunId: string;
    /** Monotonic model version under the pipeline; absent under no-signal. */
    version?: number;
    /** JSON of the test-set scores, scored once on the locked holdout: the primary proper score and the secondary metrics. */
    holdoutMetrics?: string;
    /** True when the leakage audit raised at least one flag. */
    leakageFlagged: boolean;
    /** Lifecycle status of the produced model (`Draft`), or `NoSignal` when the gate stored no-signal. */
    status: string;
    /** The `MJ: Training Snapshots` row the run trained on. */
    trainingSnapshotId?: string;
    /** The `MJ: Evaluation Protocols` row (exact version) the run was evaluated under, and that row's Version. */
    evaluationProtocolId?: string;
    evaluationProtocolVersion?: number;
    /** The stored gate outcome: model, keep-simple-baseline or no-signal. */
    gateOutcome?: string;
    /** The decision-table branch (a:beats-best-simple, a:Q15-only-model-beats-dummy, b:keep-simple-baseline, c:no-signal). */
    gateBranch?: string;
    /** The stored reason, in words generated from the stored numbers. */
    gateReason?: string;
    /** The candidate the gate ships (the model or a simple baseline); absent under no-signal. */
    shipped?: string;
}
```

```ts
// packages/AI/PredictiveStudio/Engine/src/operations/train-model.mapping.ts
import type { PredictiveStudioTrainModelOutput } from '@memberjunction/core-entities';
import { TrainingRunResultsParser } from '@memberjunction/predictive-studio-core';

export const RETIRED_TRAIN_INPUTS = ['asOf', 'labelEventDates', 'maxRows', 'primaryKeyField'] as const;


export interface TrainRunFacts {
  readonly ModelID: string | null;
  readonly ModelVersion: number | null;
  readonly ModelStatus: string | null;
  readonly RunID: string;
  readonly TrainingSnapshotID: string | null;
  readonly EvaluationProtocolID: string | null;
  /** `MJ: Evaluation Protocols.Version` of `EvaluationProtocolID`, read through the FK. */
  readonly EvaluationProtocolVersion: number | null;
  readonly ValidationResults: string | null;
}

/** TrainModel operation input/output mapping (static members on one owner, coding standards §2). */
export class TrainModelMapping {
  /** The retired inputs present in a payload, named in one message; null when the call is clean. */
  public static RefuseRetiredTrainInputs(payload: object): string | null {
    const present = RETIRED_TRAIN_INPUTS.filter((k) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(payload, k));
    return present.length === 0
      ? null
      : `TrainModel no longer accepts ${present.join(', ')}: the Prediction Unit declares the decision date and the row key, and every eligible row is read. Remove them from the call.`;
  }

  /** The operation output from the run facts and its stored envelope (no-signal keeps the old outputs, model fields absent). */
  public static TrainModelOutputFrom(f: TrainRunFacts): PredictiveStudioTrainModelOutput {
    const parsed = TrainingRunResultsParser.ParseTrainingRunResults(f.ValidationResults);
    const completed = parsed.Ok && parsed.Value.status === 'completed' ? parsed.Value : null;
    const trainer = completed?.trainer ?? null;
    const gate = completed?.gate ?? null;
    const holdoutMetrics: Record<string, number> = {};
    if (trainer !== null) {
      holdoutMetrics[trainer.holdout.primary.metric] = trainer.holdout.primary.value;
      for (const m of trainer.holdout.secondary) holdoutMetrics[m.metric] = m.value;
    }
    return {
      ...(f.ModelID === null ? {} : { modelId: f.ModelID }),
      ...(f.ModelVersion === null ? {} : { version: f.ModelVersion }),
      trainingRunId: f.RunID,
      status: f.ModelStatus || (gate?.decision.outcome === 'no-signal' ? 'NoSignal' : 'Unknown'),
      leakageFlagged: (trainer?.leakageFlags.length ?? 0) > 0,
      ...(trainer === null ? {} : { holdoutMetrics: JSON.stringify(holdoutMetrics) }),
      ...(f.TrainingSnapshotID === null ? {} : { trainingSnapshotId: f.TrainingSnapshotID }),
      ...(f.EvaluationProtocolID === null ? {} : { evaluationProtocolId: f.EvaluationProtocolID }),
      ...(f.EvaluationProtocolVersion === null ? {} : { evaluationProtocolVersion: f.EvaluationProtocolVersion }),
      ...(gate === null ? {} : { gateOutcome: gate.decision.outcome, gateBranch: gate.decision.branch, gateReason: gate.reason.text }),
      ...(gate?.decision.shipped ? { shipped: gate.decision.shipped } : {}),
    };
  }
}
```

- [ ] Step 1: Replace the body of **§5.1** (rename the heading "Evaluation Protocol and the locked holdout") with:

  > Every training run uses the **Prediction Unit** and the **Evaluation Protocol** its pipeline binds; a pipeline
  > without either is refused. Both are versioned as immutable rows: "editing" saves the next version, and a run, its
  > snapshot and its model point at the exact version rows they used. The protocol, saved before the first candidate
  > trains, declares the locked holdout (**date-carved**: every row whose date is on or after the cutoff, optionally
  > before an end date; or **rolling-origin** for forecasts, at least five origins), the inner validation over
  > development rows (repeated or grouped folds; blocked in time with a gap of at least the horizon for series), the
  > primary proper score of the unit's task family (log loss, multiclass log loss, RMSE/MAE, Poisson or Tweedie
  > deviance, MASE), the baselines, calibration, intervals, the leakage audit and the columns that never become inputs,
  > slices, the promotion margin and hard-stopping budgets. The promotion rule, leakage audit, holdout, exclusions and
  > budgets are guard fields: they are set in protocol configuration — the UI, a non-agent API caller, a scheduled job,
  > the defaults or shipped metadata — and never by an agent tool call; a protocol can optionally restrict them to
  > users (`GuardFieldsEditableBy: human-only`).
  > Candidates are ranked by their inner-fold mean with a 95% interval; the winner's inner score is optimistic and
  > labelled so. The locked holdout is read once, for the finalist, and the run stores the paired intervals against the
  > flat guess (the dummy baseline) and the simple baselines, then the **three-outcome gate**: `model` (the model beats
  > the flat guess and the best simple baseline), `keep-simple-baseline` (a simple baseline carries the signal), or
  > `no-signal`. Nothing ships when the rarest class has fewer test rows than the protocol's minimum (20 by default) or
  > a binary model's AUC interval contains 0.5. The decision and its reason are stored on the training run;
  > publishing is a separate, automated step that reads that stored decision.

**Runtime checks against MJAPI (4031) and the database** — each milestone's Step 5 lists its own (M5.11 compute
seconds, M6.7 the trainer path, M9.2 no search without a protocol, M10.3 stored decisions, M11.3 the migration); the
cumulative end-state check:

```sql
SET NOCOUNT ON;
-- every unit run has a snapshot and a v2 result; no unit run trained on a censored row
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unit_runs_without_snapshot FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun r JOIN __mj.MLTrainingPipeline p ON p.ID=r.PipelineID
 WHERE p.PredictionUnitID IS NOT NULL AND r.Status='Completed' AND r.TrainingSnapshotID IS NULL;              -- expect 0
SELECT COUNT(*) AS non_v2 FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun r JOIN __mj.MLTrainingPipeline p ON p.ID=r.PipelineID
 WHERE p.PredictionUnitID IS NOT NULL AND JSON_VALUE(r.ValidationResults,'$.schema') <> 'ps-run-results/v2'; -- expect 0
-- versions are immutable: every lineage has consecutive versions starting at 1
SELECT LineageRootID FROM __mj.PredictionUnit GROUP BY LineageRootID HAVING MIN(Version) <> 1 OR MAX(Version) <> COUNT(*); -- expect no rows
SELECT LineageRootID FROM __mj.EvaluationProtocol GROUP BY LineageRootID HAVING MIN(Version) <> 1 OR MAX(Version) <> COUNT(*); -- expect no rows
-- no unit or protocol version row was updated after it was created (Record Changes holds only Create rows for them)
SELECT e.Name, COUNT(*) FROM __mj.RecordChange rc JOIN __mj.Entity e ON e.ID=rc.EntityID
 WHERE e.Name IN ('MJ: Prediction Units','MJ: Evaluation Protocols','MJ: Training Snapshots') AND rc.Type='Update' GROUP BY e.Name;  -- expect no rows
-- trainer runs record real compute, a protocol and no artifact bytes; every unit run has a protocol
SELECT COUNT(*) AS completed_without_compute FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun WHERE Status='Completed' AND __mj_CreatedAt > '<M5 checkpoint date>' AND ComputeSeconds IS NULL; -- expect 0
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unit_runs_without_protocol FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun r JOIN __mj.MLTrainingPipeline p ON p.ID=r.PipelineID
 WHERE p.PredictionUnitID IS NOT NULL AND r.Status='Completed' AND r.EvaluationProtocolID IS NULL AND r.__mj_CreatedAt > '<M9 checkpoint date>'; -- expect 0
SELECT COUNT(*) AS artifact_bytes_stored FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun WHERE ValidationResults LIKE '%bytesBase64%';   -- expect 0
-- every completed unit run since gate records exist stores its gate decision
SELECT COUNT(*) AS completed_without_gate FROM __mj.MLTrainingRun r JOIN __mj.MLTrainingPipeline p ON p.ID=r.PipelineID
 WHERE p.PredictionUnitID IS NOT NULL AND r.Status='Completed' AND JSON_VALUE(r.ValidationResults,'$.gate.decision.outcome') IS NULL AND r.__mj_CreatedAt > '<M10 checkpoint date>'; -- expect 0
-- no pipeline left without a unit and a protocol
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unmigrated FROM __mj.MLTrainingPipeline WHERE Status <> 'Archived' AND (PredictionUnitID IS NULL OR EvaluationProtocolID IS NULL); -- expect 0
```

## 8. Refresh procedure for this PR

### 8.1 Triggers

- **(a) Kickoff** — before the plan is copied to `plans/predictive-studio/PR-3-honest-training.md`: run §8.2 in full.
- **(b) Dependency merged** — PR 2 merged (done 2026-10-26): §8.3's checks were run against the merged tree and
  this plan's fixed sections rewritten to it (§12); they run again at every refresh, and a failed check is handled by
  the refresh procedure below (the affected tasks are updated to what shipped) and recorded in §12. PR 1 merging is a soft trigger: re-check A-PR1 (Feature Values key columns) and the
  `feature-value` read filter.
- **(c) `next` merged into `ps/pr-3-honest-training`** and the merge touched any file in §5.7's anchors.
- **(d) Stale** — at a session start when the last refresh is more than 7 days old.

Procedure: `program/conventions.md` §7 (fetch → `node tools/check-anchors.mjs <this plan> <mj-checkout> <ref>` → fix
non-`ok` anchors and re-read the code → run §8.2 → update design/tasks/§9 → set `atCommit` → append §12 → STATUS).

## 9. Risks, open questions, decisions

### 9.1 Decisions (PR-local; D3-06, D3-08, D3-10 and D3-23 affect other plans and are proposed for `program/decisions.md`, §9.4)

- **D3-01** · #4166 (`sequence`) and #4104 (typed components) are not dependencies. If #4104 merges first, its
  `'action'` step kind is refused on unit pipelines (`unsupported-step-kind`). If #4166 merges first, `ProblemType
  'sequence'` pipelines stay legacy until M11, which archives them with a note: an HMM latent state has no outcome
  window and is not a Prediction Unit task. *Rejected:* adding a `sequence` `TaskKind` (no proper score, no gate).
- **D3-02** · Immutable version rows (D-014): `LineageRootID` NOT NULL, version 1 is its own root (client-supplied ID),
  `UNIQUE (LineageRootID, Version)`, no `Status` column ("current" = highest version), updates refused by `Validate()`.
- **D3-03** · Units and protocols are referenced by the **version row's ID** only; the architecture's
  `PredictionUnitVersion`/`ProtocolVersion` integer columns are dropped (the ID identifies the version; the integer
  would be a second copy). `reverifyPublish`'s protocol check (PR 4) compares IDs.
- **D3-04** · Persisted JSON shapes keep `contracts.ts`'s camelCase properties; branded string types are not used in
  product code (plain `string`), except `NonNegative`.
- **D3-05** · The outcome rule is the typed `LabelRule` union (column | next-period | child-event), not free SQL; the
  decision-date rule adds `column-offset` and `fixed` and drops `expression`. No SQL is ever built from unit JSON.
- **D3-06** · `MJ: Evaluation Protocols` has no `PipelineID`/`PredictionUnitID`; the pipeline binds one unit version
  and one protocol version, and the pipeline's `ValidateAsync` refuses a protocol whose primary-score family differs
  from the unit's task kind. *Reason:* no circular FKs, and a unit edit does not force a protocol edit.
- **D3-07** · Contract extensions: `keyField`/`ownerKeyField`; windowed-aggregate `filter`, `voidedAtField`,
  `endDateField`, `active-at`; refusals `unresolved-column`, `unsupported-step-kind`, `missing-decision-date`,
  `no-resolved-rows`; `MissingValuePolicy.impute` adds `mean`; the label-known-at-decision exclusion (needed to match
  the reference's 4,873 rows: 44 rows excluded).
- **D3-08** · "Immutable after creation" is `MJ: Entity Fields.AllowUpdateAPI = false`, confirmed by no Record Changes
  `Update` of the field after the decision instant (else `select-changes-after-decision-date`). Direct-SQL updates of
  such a field are not detected (disclosed residual risk, as architecture §7.1 discloses direct-SQL tracking toggles).
- **D3-09** · Day semantics: the as-of instant is the end of the decision day (changes strictly before
  `DecisionDate + 1 day`; child rows dated on or before the decision day), matching the reference builder.
- **D3-10** · PR 3 adds `LocalFileSystemStorage` to MJStorage and a `Local File System` provider row (priority 1000):
  snapshots need `FileStorageBase` on developer machines and CI, where no cloud provider exists. PR 4 may store
  artifacts through it in development; production deployments configure a cloud provider via
  `PS_SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_PROVIDER`.
- **D3-11** · Gate → milestone assignment (§4.2 notes): a threshold that names a gate outcome belongs to M10.
- **D3-12** · "Count declared continuous" = every value an integer ≥ 0, 0 present, fewer than 50 distinct values.
- **D3-13** · `ComputeSeconds` is always recorded (M5.11); `ComputeCost = ComputeSeconds × PS_COMPUTE_USD_PER_SECOND`
  and is NULL (unknown) when the rate is not configured — never a hard-coded 0 (D3-32).
- **D3-14** · Legacy (unit-less) pipelines keep training until M11 migrates them, except that a non-`none`
  `AsOfStrategy` is refused (`unit-required`); M11 then removes the legacy path.
- **D3-15** · The provenance file is not part of the content hash (identical data → one snapshot).
- **D3-16** · PR 3 adds the C1 raw corpus (person-periods and dated activity) to the truth suite; PR 2 ships no copy of
  the reference's resolved parquet (M5.2 commits one to `fixtures/real/`, D3-73; M2.1 reads ps-review's).
- **D3-17** · In a forecast unit, a column of the row itself is accepted only with a declared `PeriodOffsets` ≥ the
  horizon; otherwise it is refused as `future-period-lag` naming it. A false declaration is caught by M7's
  time-shifted-label audit.
- **D3-18** · `TrainingSnapshot.EvaluationProtocolID` and `MLTrainingRun.EvaluationProtocolID` are NULL-able in the
  schema (legacy runs; snapshots before M9); M9/M11 refuse a run without a protocol in code.
- **D3-20** · The milestones M5–M11 were drafted separately and merged into this plan on 2026-10-12 (§12). The merge
  applied §5.1's names everywhere: `MLTrainingRun.TrainingSnapshotID`/`EvaluationProtocolID` (never
  `SnapshotID`/`ProtocolID`), no `ProtocolVersion`/`PredictionUnitVersion` columns (versions are read through the FK,
  D3-03), no `PipelineID`/`PredictionUnitID` on protocols (D3-06), version-1 rows with `LineageRootID = ID`, the
  product unit and protocol types (`PredictionUnitSpec`, `EvaluationProtocolSpec`) instead of contracts.ts's
  `PredictionUnit`/`EvaluationProtocol`, and plain strings instead of branded primitives (D3-04).
- **D3-21** · Gate flips follow §4.2 exactly; a gate's pytest node may be written in an earlier milestone (G2.30 in
  M5.12; G2.4, G2.1–G2.3, G2.8 in M6.8) and the gate is flipped by its owner (M9.6, M10.5). Each gate has exactly one
  check (§4.1). Where a later milestone also checks a gate it does not own (M9.1 for G2.28; M10.5 for G2.21, G2.33,
  G2.36, G2.37), the check is additional coverage and is marked so; pytest tests that are not a gate's measured node
  carry `@pytest.mark.covers("<testName>")` instead of `@pytest.mark.gate(...)`. *Rejected:* flipping a gate where its
  test was first written, which would have flipped G2.30, G2.1–G2.4 and G2.8 before the milestones that own their
  behaviour.
- **D3-22** · *(Mechanism superseded by D3-61, 2026-10-26; the rule stands.)* A gate measured by sidecar pytest
  nodes passes only when every case of its nodes passed; a node not collected, skipped or errored fails it (a renamed
  node can never pass). The JUnit report is read, not pytest's exit code (exit 1 cannot tell a failed assertion from a
  crash in a fixture).
- **D3-23** · The stored gate outcome of a run is TypeScript's: Core `DecideGuardedGate(StoredGateIntervalsFromResult(result), protocol.promotion.margin, guards)`, i.e. `DecideGate`
  over `GateInputsFromIntervals` followed by `GateRules.ApplyGateGuards` (M10.1–M10.3). The
  sidecar's `app/gate.py` (M6.3) keeps refpipe's `gate_decision` verbatim (plus the contract-shaped `gate_record` and
  `run_gate`) because the sidecar must choose which artifacts to return and the pytest gates measure it; M10.3
  refuses a run whose sidecar decision differs from `DecideGate` before guards (`sidecar-gate-mismatch`). M10.2's parity
  test covers TypeScript vs the sidecar copy and TypeScript vs refpipe (5,000 + 20,000 seeded cases, 0 mismatches).
  Proposed for `program/decisions.md` as D-026. *Rejected:* the sidecar's decision as the stored outcome (PR 4's
  `reverifyPublish` re-derives in TypeScript; two authorities would drift); a second `gate.py` in M10.
- **D3-24** · Exported functions are PascalCase, including the ported contract functions: `DecideGate`
  (contracts.ts `decideGate`), `GateInputsFromIntervals`, `BeatsByMargin`, `ToNonNegative`. Wire-shape members keep
  contracts.ts camelCase (D3-04) with the naming gate's reviewed-exception marker. No brand types or `As*` producers.
- **D3-25** · Core module map: `evaluation-protocol.ts` (M1) gains `EvaluationProtocolSpec` and
  `EvaluationProtocol.ParseEvaluationProtocolRow` in M5.1, not M9 — the trainer request (M5) carries the parsed protocol; `gate.ts` holds
  the gate types from M5.1 and the gate functions from M10.1; `trainer-contract.ts` (M5.1) holds C4; there is no
  `ps-contracts.ts` or `contract-primitives.ts`; `Interval`/`MetricWithInterval`/`METRIC_DIRECTION` stay in
  `evaluation-protocol.ts` and `TaskType` in `task-type.ts`.
- **D3-26** · The snapshot matrix header is the trainer's input format (`ps-snapshot-matrix/v1`, M4.2): feature
  columns with source column and full `ColumnEncoding`, the label column, the optional incumbent-score column
  (`__ps_incumbent_score`, evaluated by Core `IncumbentExpressions.EvaluateIncumbentExpression` from the unit's `scoreExpression`; never SQL,
  D3-05) and slice columns (`__ps_slice:<field>`), the unit's `DecisionSpec`, and the legacy feature schema and
  preprocessing; matrix row i is manifest line i. The header is inside `MatrixSha256`, so it is fingerprinted.
  `__ps_reference_score` is written only by test fixtures. *Rejected:* a second single-JSON matrix format written for
  the sidecar (two formats of one snapshot); carrying encodings in `TrainerRequest` (the snapshot would not be
  self-describing for retraining).
- **D3-27** · Ownership of the engine–trainer wiring: M6.7 builds `TrainerRequest`, calls `RunTrainer`, applies the
  result and stores `trainer`/`trainerRequest` for unit pipelines bound to a protocol (the M4 `SnapshotRetrainer.TrainOnSnapshot` path
  serves the others); M9.2 requires a protocol for every unit pipeline and removes `SnapshotRetrainer.TrainOnSnapshot` from the unit path;
  M10.3 stores the TypeScript gate decision and creates the model row from the shipped artifact; M11.3 migrates legacy
  pipelines and deletes the legacy path (`/train`, `TrainRequest`/`TrainResponse`, `ISidecarTrainer.train`,
  `SnapshotRetrainer.TrainOnSnapshot`, `LegacyRequestConfig`, `LegacyTrainerMetrics`). *Rejected:* wiring in M5 (no `/trainer` route
  exists until M6.5) or in M9 (M6–M8 gates would then measure an engine path that does not exist).
- **D3-28** · `ValidationResults` (`ps-run-results/v2`) grows by milestone: `legacyRequest` (M4), `trainer:
  StoredTrainerResult` and `trainerRequest: TrainerRequestConfig` (M6.7), `carve` (M9.3), `gate: StoredGateRecord`
  (M10.3); M11.3 drops `legacy`/`legacyRequest`. Artifact bytes are never stored in it: artifacts are `MJ: Files`
  rows, referenced by `StoredArtifactRef.fileId`. Refusal stages `trainer` (`trainer-failed`, `lineage-incomplete`,
  M6.7) and `gate` (`sidecar-gate-mismatch`, M10.3) extend `TrainingRefusal`.
- **D3-29** · Contract extensions (PR-local; proposed diffs for `reference/contracts/contracts.ts` in §9.4):
  E1 `CandidateSpec.driverKey`; E2 the trainer names the column of a time-shifted-label flag with a paired
  `single-feature-auc` flag (no type change); E3 `TrainerResult.completed.forecast: ForecastEvaluation | null`;
  E4 `TrainerResult.completed.innerSplitContrast: SplitContrast | null`; E5
  `TrainerResult.completed.predictionIntervalCoverage: readonly PredictionIntervalCoverage[]` (one per nominal level,
  because `PredictionIntervalSpec.nominalCoverage` is a list and G2.17 checks 80% and 90%); E6 the date-carved
  `HoldoutSplit` gains `holdoutEnd: string | null` (M9.3 reproduces C1's 1,205 test keys); E7
  `TrainerRequest.protocol` is `EvaluationProtocolSpec` (no `pipeline`/`unit`, D3-06). Deviations: D1
  `CalibrationReport.method` is the fitted map's method when the map was applied, else the protocol's declared kind;
  D2 `ReturnedArtifact.sha256` is the SHA-256 of the decoded envelope bytes (what `MJ: Files` stores).
- **D3-30** · The pipeline's `EvaluationProtocolID` names the protocol version a run uses. Unit-independent protocol
  rules run in the protocol entity's `ValidateAsync`; unit-dependent rules (`EvaluationProtocolRules.ValidateProtocolForUnit`: primary-score
  family = task kind, holdout kind fits the task, lags/rolling windows/inner gap ≥ horizon) run in the pipeline's
  `ValidateAsync` and again at training (M9.1–M9.2).
- **D3-31** · Simple-member names are fixed: `dummy`, `oneFeature`, `glm`, `naive`, `seasonalNaive`,
  `heuristic:<IncumbentHeuristic.name>`; comparisons are keyed `modelVsDummy`, `<member>VsDummy`, `modelVs:<member>`;
  a candidate may not use a member name or the `heuristic:` prefix (HTTP 400).
- **D3-32** · `ComputeSeconds` is the trainer's `computeSeconds` (or the legacy `duration_sec`); `ComputeCost` is
  `ComputeSeconds × PS_COMPUTE_USD_PER_SECOND`, NULL when the rate is not configured (`compute-cost.ts`, M5.11).
- **D3-33** · The minority-class guard reads the protocol's `MinMinorityClassRows` (default 20), not a constant.
- **D3-34** · Sidecar gate tests run in PR 2's TruthSuite venv through `PREDICTIVE_STUDIO_PYTHON`; the sidecar venv
  stays product-only. *Rejected:* adding pyarrow to the sidecar. *(2026-10-26: the TruthSuite venv PR 2 shipped is the
  sidecar's pins plus mypy, without pyarrow or statsmodels, §8.3 A-PR2-VENV; M2.1 Step 0 pins `pyarrow` and M5.2
  `statsmodels` there, D3-73.)*
- **D3-35** · PR 2's C5.2 already makes legacy `kfold`/`holdout` out-of-sample (F-SC-1 is PR 2's finding); M5.10
  only seeds the legacy estimators and accepts the catalog MLP default (F-SC-2, F-SC-3).
- **D3-36** · `HoldoutSplit` gains `{ kind: 'seeded-random', fraction }` for units whose decision date is `fixed`
  (cross-sectional scenarios such as C2 and R3 cannot be carved by date): a row is in the locked holdout when the
  FNV-1a hash of `<seed>:<rowId>` divided by 2^32 is below `fraction`. M9.3 extends M1.2's shape check, M5.1's
  `EvaluationProtocol.ParseEvaluationProtocolRow`, the sidecar's pydantic mirror and `run.refuse_invalid`. The date-carved `dateColumn` is
  the unit row's decision date when it is `DecisionDate`, else the unit row's own field (W6 carves on `StartDate`);
  rows on or after `holdoutEnd` are left out of the snapshot. *Rejected:* the trailing-fraction carve in read order.
- **D3-37** (amended by D3-42, D3-43, D3-44) · The migration of legacy pipelines (M11.3) maps `AsOfStrategy` column
  mode to a column decision date with a 1-day window and censoring `now`; no as-of to a fixed decision date that
  advances to each run's day (D3-43) with a seeded-random holdout of the legacy share; it archives offset as-of,
  single-valued targets, `sequence` pipelines (D3-01) and pipelines whose date column is constant (reason appended to
  `Description`); binary class order is the legacy encoder's ordinal string order and the adverse class comes from the
  pipeline's declared outcome semantics, else the pipeline is held (D3-42); regression becomes `continuous`;
  `LockedHoldoutFraction` becomes a trailing-share date cutoff; k-fold becomes repeated folds; the deny lists become
  `Exclusions`. The release step runs a dry run, the real run and their agreement check (D3-44).
- **D3-38** · `PredictiveStudio.TrainModel` drops `asOf`, `labelEventDates`, `maxRows` and `primaryKeyField` from its
  input type (moved to `RetiredTrainModelInputs`, refused by name when sent) and adds read-only outputs
  `trainingSnapshotId`, `evaluationProtocolId`, `evaluationProtocolVersion` (read through the FK), `gateOutcome`,
  `gateBranch`, `gateReason`, `shipped` (M11.4).
- **D3-39** · *(Superseded by D3-59, 2026-10-26, for the gate mechanism.)* PR 3's gates drive the product through
  PR 2's truth-suite harness; the capabilities it lacks are added to `TruthHarness` (`ReadWorldTruth`, `SampleRowIds`,
  `ResolveProvenance`, `UseSuiteSidecar`); W8's `sidecar-16gb` requirement is lifted by F-L4-5. *Rejected:* an adapter
  that rebuilds a PR-3-specific gate context from the harness (a second API to keep in step).
- **D3-40** · `MJ: Evaluation Protocols.GuardFieldsEditableBy` is `'non-agent' | 'human-only'`, default `'non-agent'`
  (D-029: a human step is an optional setting, never a requirement). The guard fields are holdout, promotion, leakage
  audit, exclusions, budgets and the setting itself (`GUARD_FIELDS`). Under `non-agent` every author except an agent
  tool call (`Actor.kind === 'agent'`) — a user, a non-agent API caller, a scheduled job, the system's defaults, shipped
  metadata — may change them in a new version; an agent may author protocols (PR 5's draft Actions) and change any
  other field, but not relax its own guardrails (G3.11, D-031's wording). Under `human-only` only a user-authored version
  changes them. The setting in force is the previous version's, so a version cannot lift its own restriction. Every
  author's version passes the same validation (`EvaluationProtocol.GetEvaluationProtocolShapeProblems`, `EvaluationProtocol.ParseEvaluationProtocolRow`,
  `EvaluationProtocolRules.ValidateEvaluationProtocol`, `EvaluationProtocolRules.ValidateProtocolForUnit`). One refusal kind, `guard-field-edited-by-disallowed-author
  {Fields, Author, Setting}`; the check is `MayEditGuardFields(author, setting)`. Defaults
  (`EvaluationProtocolRules.DefaultEvaluationProtocolDraft`), the migration and shipped protocols set the fields automatically. *Rejected:*
  human-only as the only value (makes every automated protocol change wait for a person); any author including agents
  (an agent could loosen the gate it is graded by).
- **D3-41** · PR 3 has no leakage-flag override: every flagged source column is excluded from every candidate and
  baseline automatically and recorded in the run's `leakageFlags` (M7). A false positive is answered by protocol
  configuration — a new protocol version with a different `singleFeatureHeldOutAucMax` (validated in (0.5, 1]) or
  `Exclusions`, authored under D3-40 — never per run and never by an agent tool call. G2.9's quoted clause "the recorded
  sign-off for an override is Phase 3" belongs to PR 4's publish record (D-029: approver `automated-gate` or a named
  user; a human sign-off only as the optional `requiresHumanSignOff`). *Rejected:* a per-run override field (an
  unversioned way around the audit).
- **D3-42** · A migrated binary unit's adverse class is derived, not chosen: the legacy score was P(`classOrder[1]`)
  with `classOrder` the sidecar's `LabelEncoder` order over `str(value)` (ordinal string order), and the pipeline
  declared its meaning in `OutcomeConfig`. `LegacyPipelines.LegacyAdverseClass` reads, in the legacy engine's precedence, the pipeline's
  explicit config, the newest (Published first) model's lineage config, then `ResolveOutcomeConfig`'s target-name
  polarity; within a source a single red class, else a single green class's other class, else `Polarity`
  (`adverse` → index 1, `positive` → index 0) decides. When nothing decides, the pipeline is **held**: unchanged
  status, published models keep scoring, training refused with the reason, migrated by a later run of the Action
  (any actor may run it — an agent through the Action, a scheduled job, the release step) once its `OutcomeConfig`
  declares the polarity. The deciding source and evidence are stored in the report and the unit's `Description`.
  Multiclass adverse indices are the red-styled classes of the first source that styles any. *Rejected:* the
  alphabetically first class (silently wrong for half of the targets); archiving undecidable pipelines (stops models
  that are serving).
- **D3-43** · A legacy pipeline with no as-of becomes a unit whose fixed decision date advances: `DecisionDateRule`
  `fixed` gains optional `advance: 'each-run'`; before each run `DecisionDateAdvance.AdvanceFixedDecisionDate` saves the next unit version
  with the run's UTC day (censoring cutoff moved by window + gap), authored `{kind:'system', component:
  'decision-date-advance'}`, and binds the pipeline to it — only when the bound version is the lineage's newest.
  Each run reads features as they stand that day (the legacy behaviour) and each model references the exact version.
  The protocol holdout is `seeded-random` (D3-36), which also fixes the earlier `__mj_CreatedAt` date carve that
  `EvaluationProtocolRules.ValidateProtocolForUnit` refuses for a fixed-date unit. *Rejected:* a date frozen at migration day (later runs never
  see new records); `__mj_CreatedAt` as the decision date (features as of creation change what the model means).
- **D3-44** · The pipeline migration runs without a reader: the release step runs the Action as a dry run and as the
  real run, requires `FailedCount` 0 and equal counts, and checks that the unbound non-archived pipelines number
  `HeldCount` (M11.3 Step 7). The runtime check is a rig with assertions (`ps-pipeline-migration-check.ts`). *Rejected:*
  "review the dry-run report, then apply" (a human gate).
- **D3-45** · UI runtime checks are Playwright tests with assertions (`e2e/specs/ps-honest-training.spec.ts`, M10.4
  and M11.2), run against the agent's own MJAPI/Explorer with the profile primed by `e2e/overlay/prime-auth.mjs`;
  readability in light and dark themes is an axe `color-contrast` assertion. The model form's evaluation panel leads
  the overview panel (sortKey 90 < 100), asserted by the spec. *Rejected:* screenshots in the handoff (no assertion).
- **D3-46** · §9.3's questions are resolved with implemented defaults (decisions D3-01, D3-36, D3-40…D3-44 and the
  defaults stated there); none blocks execution or waits for a person. The D-062 scope questions (Q3-15, Q3-16,
  Q3-17) waited for the owner and are decided (D3-73, D3-74).
- **D3-47** · Supersedes D3-24's free-function form (program D-037, controller ruling PR3-R2): the ported contract
  functions are public statics of their owning class with no free-function aliases: `GateRules.DecideGate`,
  `GateRules.GateInputsFromIntervals`, `GateRules.BeatsByMargin`, `GateRules.DecideGuardedGate`,
  `EvaluationProtocol.ToNonNegative`, `TaskTypeRules.ScoreSemantics`. D3-23's `DecideGuardedGate`/`DecideGate` and
  D3-24's PascalCase rule otherwise stand. *Rejected:* exported functions beside a class (two call forms).

Shifts are taken row by row within an entity, as refpipe does (owner flag y).
- **D3-133** · Every feature column of a source column is audited (derived columns from `AsOfFeatureAssembler.ColumnsFor` included) and the source is flagged when any of them is, with evidence kept per column (Q5); identifier columns are flagged `high-cardinality-id` (Q18). The distinct-ratio rule applies to columns declared categorical or identifier, where refpipe applies it to every non-numeric column; the difference is documented in `audit.py`, and the C4 gate node holds the port to refpipe's audit (identical flags, max |evidence − `scoreByShift`| 4.70e-11 ≤ 1e-10) (Q16). An exact tie between shifts resolves in refpipe's string order — same period, next period, previous period — so a copy of a label that never changes within an entity is a same-period proxy, not a lag (M7.1 review C1). One owner calls the audit: `run._dev_audit`, used by the run and by the parity node (M7.4 review M1).
- **D3-134** · The implausible-gain rule (planted reference score, binary only): drop-column trials score with `trainer.cross_validate` on the finished selection's folds, no refit per trial; after the explaining source columns are excluded and selection runs again, `beats_reference` runs once more, and a candidate that still beats the reference fails the run at `inner-cv` (Q4).
- **D3-135** · One held-out permutation-importance implementation, `importance.permutation_importance` (one row permutation per source column, 5 repeats, paired-bootstrap interval through `intervals.paired_bootstrap`) (Q10). The trainer runs it inside the holdout stage before the clock's last check, on the holdout rows with the protocol's resamples, level and resampling units, and it describes the finalist even when the gate ships a simple baseline (Q3). The legacy `/train` path calls it through a source map read from the fitted preprocessing ops (`col=level`, `col__missing` → `col`), with no bootstrap draws, and reports shares of the positive loss increase as kind `held_out_permutation`; below 2 locked-holdout rows it reports `{}`/`none`. `importance_type="gain"` is not set on LightGBM: nothing reads `feature_importances_` once importance is held-out permutation on both paths, so it would be dead configuration; the permutation change closes F-SC-9b (biased split-count importance) (Q11).
- **D3-136** · Per-row drivers are `coef × (z − z̄)` against the mean encoded training row. A v2 artifact carries the mean in its envelope (`driverBaseline` with the aligned `transformedColumns`; never pickled on the predictor); the legacy format stashes it on the estimator as `mj_driver_baseline_`, its only owner. A missing or misaligned mean gives no driver, never an uncentred one; one ranking rule (`trainer.top_signed_drivers`) serves both paths (Q8, M7 close self-audit).

G2.10: `run` keeps flagged sources; `beats_reference` returns False), G2.40 the plan's own (importance on training rows) (Q6, Q7). Exit counts are restated from measurements (Q15). *Rejected:* rewording shipped tests to fit the table.
- **D3-138** · A forecast's artifacts are a typed union: `artifacts_v2.build` and `artifacts.load_v2_shippable` accept `TrainedPredictor | SeriesModel | SeriesBaseline` (the explicit `SHIPPABLE_TYPES` allow-set; a training-window-mean series baseline is the forecast gate's dummy and is refused as a yardstick, as the dummy and the incumbent heuristic are by name), and the restricted unpickler's allow-list gains `app.temporal.SeriesModel`/`SeriesBaseline`. `/predict` scores rows, so `load_v2_envelope` refuses a series envelope with the typed `SeriesForecasterNotServedError` and the route answers 400; serving forecasts is not built (owner flag aa) (M8 preflight Q1).
- **D3-139** · What a forecast run does not do, each stated in `forecast.py`'s or `run.py`'s docstring: it skips the leakage audit (a forecast snapshot is one series, so one entity, and the audit's grouped folds need at least 5 entities — it could only score NaN) (Q2); it reports `importance=[]` (owner flag bb) (Q3) and `incumbentDiff=null` (owner flag cc) (Q18); it trains one series per snapshot and refuses a panel at load-snapshot with a message naming the limitation (owner flag dd) (Q20).
- **D3-140** · How a forecast reads its protocol: the primary score is honoured (`rmse` → unscaled errors and an RMSE aggregate; `mase` → errors scaled by each origin's own in-sample seasonal-naive MAE), and the gate runs on the same per-row losses (Q4); interval and lower-bound levels come from `intervals.level` and `promotion.lowerBoundLevel`; the Ljung–Box veto's alpha from `residualDiagnostics.ljungBoxAlpha`, else the named constant 0.05, on refpipe's lag rule min(24, n / 5); reported diagnostics use `acfLags` (Q5). Refused with 400 before anything is fitted: no declared seasonal-naive baseline (it sets the MASE scale and is a gate member) (Q5); `intervals.method` other than `block-bootstrap` (the gate and every interval resample whole origins; `pairedTest` is not constrained, the Diebold–Mariano test against seasonal naive is always reported beside the comparisons, and the plan's own M9 default gives forecast block-bootstrap with paired-bootstrap) (M8.2 Q-a); declared `predictionIntervals` (the contract's methods are split-conformal | quantile, not the series models' Gaussian h-step intervals; owner flag ff; `SeriesModel.interval` stays, tested, the plan's interface) (M8.2 Q-b); declared slices (M8.2 I4). `innerValidation` is ignored on a forecast — the inner origins are its inner validation — and documented.
- **D3-141** · One owner per thing and one failure surface on the forecast path: `temporal.py` owns the rolling-origin design, per-origin scoring and the baseline forecasts, and `forecast.py` consumes them without re-implementing any (Q9). The design is validated up front — every outer and inner training window must be longer than the season, else `failed`/`load-snapshot` naming the origin; a zero MASE scale fails `holdout` naming the origin; the result passes `refuse_non_finite`; `NotShippableError` becomes `failed`/`holdout`; nothing but `TrainerFailure` leaves the path (Q10). A snapshot whose period ordinals repeat or skip is refused at load-snapshot naming the period (Q11).
- **D3-142** · The rolling-origin design is refpipe's: later origins train on earlier origins' test periods (each forecasts only periods after its own window) and the returned artifacts are fitted on the whole series (Q12). ### 9.2 Risks

| Id | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| R3-01 | PR 2 as merged differs from what this plan consumes. | §8.3's checks against the merged tree at every refresh, each failure handled by the refresh procedure; the gate code is confined to the check files and `ps-gates/` of `integration-test-suite` (§2.7), the four harness members of §5.4, `src/fixtures/unit-fixtures.ts` and `src/fixtures/c1-corpus-loader.ts`, plus the trainer fixture's planted-truth readers (M5.3). |
| R3-02 | Complete reads of `MJ: Record Changes` per entity are slow on large tracked entities. | Read only entities a unit pipeline selects as `record-changes`; M12.2 measures; if one read exceeds 60 s on the C1/W worlds, add a `RecordID IN` batching path to `RunViewRecordHistoryReader` (same results, verified by the M3.2 tests). |
| R3-03 | The in-process gate assemblies (G1.4, G1.12, G1.11) run over the GraphQL provider and may be slow. | They read the same rows the server reads; M12 records each row's run time and sets its `MaxExecutionTimeMS` from it. |
| R3-04 | The C1 as-of feature set omits the reference's `prior_lapse` (no windowed form), which could change C1's gate outcome (G2.7, M10) and the C1 baselines. | M10 compares PS's C1 one-feature/GLM scores with the reference's; if G2.7 fails for this reason, add a `max-gap-days` aggregate (largest gap between consecutive child dates in the window) and record a decision. |
| R3-05 | Local-disk snapshots are lost with the disk and unreadable from other hosts. | D3-10; deployment guide (M12.4) states that multi-host installs must point `PS_SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` at a cloud provider. |
| R3-06 | #4166 lands mid-PR and widens `ProblemType`. | D3-01, M1.5 step 4, assumption check A-4166. |
| R3-07 | `DATE` columns arrive as `Date` objects (server) or strings (GraphQL client); a time-zone shift would move decision days. | `UtcDay.ToUtcDay` reads strings by their date part and `Date`s by UTC components; M2.3 Step 5 checks the exact C1 counts, which any shift would break. |
| R3-08 | The W-world decision day (1 December) is a fixture convention. | It is declared in the unit, not in code; the W gates measure rows and calibration, not the convention. |
| R3-09 | PR 1 not merged → Feature Values lack the key columns PR 5 pins on. | The pinned read uses only columns on `next` plus PR 3's; A-PR1 adds filters when PR 1 lands. |
| R3-10 | The sidecar's AR(1) is fitted by conditional least squares (statsmodels is not a sidecar dependency): T4 outer MASE 0.6229 [0.4873, 0.7796] against refpipe's ARIMA 0.6242 [0.4854, 0.7821]. | Both lie inside G2.11's interval; owner M8. Decided: no statsmodels in the sidecar while G2.11 passes; if M8's G2.11 measurement falls outside the interval, the executing agent adds a pinned `statsmodels` to the sidecar and records the decision in §9.1. |
| R3-11 | The 400-seed gates (G2.1–G2.3, G2.13, G2.35; G2.4 at 60 seeds) were not measured at full seed count, and PR 2 shipped no 400-seed set (`SeedSetName` is `'base' \| 't2'`; M5.2 adds `n400`, D3-73). Measured ≈ 0.5 s per W2 seed per worker, so ≈ 4–8 min per 400-seed gate on 8 workers; five 400-seed sets add five × 400 seed directories to `$TRUTH_DATA_DIR`. | They form `Predictive Studio Gates — Training (statistical)`, run before merge on the final head (D3-63); M12 records wall time and cache size. |
| R3-12 | Incumbent models trained before PR 3 are legacy (`joblib`) envelopes the trainer cannot load (stage `holdout`, "is not a v2 predictor"). | The engine sends `incumbent: null` for an incumbent without `MJ: Evaluation Protocols` lineage and the run records that no incumbent comparison was made; PR 4's automated publish reads that record (D-029: no human sign-off unless the protocol opts into `requiresHumanSignOff`; owner PR 4). |
| R3-13 | M6's calibration rule also applies the map when it repairs an out-of-range slope (refpipe applies it only when out-of-fold log loss drops); LightGBM on W1 s43 still measures slope 0.7999 and is hidden. | Decided: keep the repair while G2.39 passes (it allows hidden families); if G2.39 fails because of it, the executing agent deletes `_slope_repaired` (refpipe's rule only) and records it in §9.1 (owner M6). |
| R3-14 | `run_forecast` evaluates one series per snapshot; a multi-entity forecast is evaluated as a date-carved panel (T2p) and fails `load-snapshot` for more than one entity on the rolling-origin path. | Declared limit; owner M8. |
| R3-15 | Out-of-time slices are keyed by decision-date year (or the manifest `period`), and M9.3's `HoldoutCarve.HoldoutPeriods` must use the same buckets, or M10.3's slice coverage reports false gaps. | M9.3 copies the sidecar's bucketing rule (`slice_results`); M10.3's test checks both. |
| R3-16 | A renamed pytest node makes its gate fail (`NotCollected` non-empty in `PsGatePytest.Run`'s result), never pass. | Intended (D3-22, D3-61); renaming a gate's node edits its check file in the same commit. |
| R3-17 | `data:` URLs from `InMemorySnapshotFileStore` carry the whole matrix in the request; `file://` URLs from `LocalFileSystemStorage` work only when the sidecar runs on the MJAPI host. | `data:` only in tests; a remote sidecar needs a cloud provider in `PS_SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_PROVIDER` (§8.2 A-LOCAL-URL). |

The D-062 scope questions (Q3-15, Q3-16, Q3-17) waited for the owner's explicit yes; the owner decided them on
2026-10-26 (D3-73, D3-74).

Product-direction questions keep a working automated default; the others are decided.

- Q3-1 (decided): Prediction Units and Evaluation Protocols appear both in the Studio's "Define" group (sections
  `units`, `protocols`) and as record panels on the pipeline (M11.2). Default (implemented): as built.
- Q3-2 (product direction): scoring a `grain-x-periods` unit model in production — which period's decision date applies
  to a person scored "now". Default (implemented): the scored row is a period row and its own decision date applies
  (`'unit-rule'`); PR 4 owns the scoring service's rule.
- Q3-3 (product direction): production storage for snapshots. Default (implemented): the configured provider named by
  `PS_SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_PROVIDER`; retention indefinite (snapshots are model lineage).
- Q3-4 (decided, D3-01): #4166's `sequence` pipelines are archived by M11.3 with the reason.
- Q3-5 (product direction): a keep-simple-baseline outcome whose shipped member is the incumbent heuristic has no
  artifact. Default (implemented): M10.3 stores the decision and creates no model row; PR 4 owns delivering a heuristic
  (recommended there: a "rule model" row type).
- Q3-6 (decided): multiclass `/predict` gains `probabilities` + `classOrder` additively (F-L4-6, M6.5); PR 4 owns
  scoring semantics (seam `c6-multiclass`).
- Q3-7 (product direction): the new-entity report is carved and stored by M9.3 but not scored separately. Default
  (implemented): carve and stored summary only; PR 4 owns scoring it.
- Q3-8 (product direction): per-experiment feature sets. Default (implemented): candidates differ by algorithm and
  hyperparameters only, and the builder logs feature-set proposals as not applied (M9.4); PR 5 owns them.
- Q3-9 (decided): `ValidationStrategy` / `LeakageGuard` / `AsOfStrategy` stay on the pipeline, deprecated and read by
  nothing after M11.3; dropping them is a later breaking-change PR under the publish-no-break policy, outside this program.
- Q3-10 (decided): the migration's release step is recorded by M11.3 Step 7 in `program/release-procedure.md` (D3-44).
- Q3-11 (decided): D-024 puts the decision-table and interval parity loops in PR 3 (M10.2) and the 46 run-time checks
  of `deliver`/`compareToIncumbent`/`reverifyPublish`/`decideStatusWrite` in PR 4; PR 4's kickoff refresh updates its §3
  note (an instruction to that refresh, M12.7).
- Q3-12 (decided, D3-42, D3-43): migrated binary units take the adverse class their pipeline already declared or are
  held with the reason; units without dates advance their decision date to each run's day.
- Q3-13 (decided): G2.25's new-entity fraction is 0.15; the reference's 2,268 / 367 rows are recorded as measured
  values only, since the threshold needs 0 shared keys (M9.6).
- Q3-14 (decided): M11.3 creates the unit, then the protocol, then saves the pipeline without a transaction; a failed
  pipeline save leaves immutable orphan rows that nothing trains on, listed in the report row (`failed`, with both ids).

  Decision (D3-74): M11.2 creates `packages/Angular/Explorer/dashboards/src/PredictiveStudio/record-panels/ps-protocol-panels.ts`
  and does not modify `ng-core-entity-forms`.
- Q3-16 (scope, D-062 (1)/(2); decided by the owner 2026-10-26 → D3-73): PR 2 as merged ships no `truthsuite.paths`, no `truthsuite.refpipe`, no
  `fixtures/reference/p5-golden.json`, no `fixtures/real/`, no 400-seed set and no `pyarrow`/`statsmodels` in either

## 10. PR description draft

> **Predictive Studio: honest training — Prediction Units, as-of assembly, Training Snapshots, Evaluation Protocols,
> Trainer/Evaluator, three-outcome gate**
>
> Plan: `plans/predictive-studio/PR-3-honest-training.md` (first commit). Part 3 of 6 of the Predictive Studio rebuild.
>
> **What changes.** A pipeline now trains on a declared **Prediction Unit** — what one row is, its decision date, the
> outcome rule and window, censoring, and the task type — instead of every row of an entity as it stands today. Rows
> whose outcome is not yet known are excluded and counted. Every input is assembled **as of each row's decision date**
> from dated history (Record Changes replay with coverage checks, immutable fields, windowed aggregates over dated
> child tables, declared series lags); nothing is coerced to 0.0; one function serves training and scoring. Each run
> freezes its data in an immutable, fingerprinted **Training Snapshot** (three files in MJ storage) that retrains
> reproducibly. An **Evaluation Protocol**, saved before any search, fixes the date-carved locked holdout, inner
> validation, proper primary score, baselines, intervals, calibration, leakage audit and promotion margin; the
> rewritten sidecar evaluation loop runs it and the run stores a three-outcome gate decision (`model`,
> `keep-simple-baseline`, `no-signal`) with the paired intervals behind it. The trust verdict is rebuilt on that
> decision.
>
> **Schema.** New `MJ: Prediction Units`, `MJ: Evaluation Protocols`, `MJ: Training Snapshots` (immutable version rows,
> Record Changes audited); new columns on `MJ: ML Training Pipelines`, `MJ: ML Training Runs`, `MJ: Feature Values`.
> One migration (`V<yyyymmddhhmm>__v6.2.x__PS_Honest_Training_Schema.sql`, the name M1.3 wrote) with its CodeGen output. New storage driver
> `Local File System Storage`. Existing pipelines are migrated to a unit and a protocol (M11).
>
> **Acceptance.** 53 planted-truth gates (Phase 1: 12, Phase 2: 41) land Active in their suites and pass; PR 2's
> Containment suite stays 10 of 10; deterministic integration tier green with mutation tests. Closes 51 assessment
> findings (S0: F-L4-1, F-L4-3, F-LK-1, F-SCN-1, F-SEL-2, F-TR-1).
>
> **Release notes (long-stable behaviour this PR changes; conventions §5a).**
> - *Holdout.* Training no longer holds out the trailing `LockedHoldoutFraction` of rows in read order; the holdout is
>   the protocol's date-carved cut (or a seeded-random share for units with one decision date, or the last rolling
>   origins for forecasts). Holdout scores of a retrained model are not comparable with the same pipeline's earlier
>   models. *Regression strategy:* G2.6 `C1 → S6.1` (1,205 reference keys, 0 in training), the carve unit tests (M9.3),
>   order-independence test, and the M9.3 runtime check of the stored carve.
> - *Trust verdict.* `TrustVerdicts.DeriveTrustVerdict` no longer grades AUC/R² bands or falls back to in-sample metrics; it renders
>   the gate decision stored on the training run. A model trained before this PR has no stored decision: it shows "Not
>   evaluated yet" and the business catalog does not open it. *Remediation:* retrain it through its migrated pipeline
>   (the run stores the decision); PR 4 re-verifies at publish. *Regression strategy:* PR 2's G0.11/G0.12 stay green on
>   the stored decision (M10.4 Step 4), the trust and business-catalog tests, and the Playwright spec of M10.4/M11.2.
> - *Pipelines.* The `MJ: ML Training Pipelines` rows are migrated once (M11.3, release step D3-44): each gets a version-1
>   Prediction Unit and Evaluation Protocol, or is archived (offset as-of, sequence, single-valued target) or held
>   (adverse class undetermined) with the reason in its `Description`. *Remediation for held pipelines:* declare
>   `OutcomeConfig.Polarity` (or `OutcomeStyles`) and run the Action again; their published models keep scoring
>   through the legacy scoring path meanwhile (§5.5). The release step asserts dry run = real run and
>   `Unbound = HeldCount`.
> - *Training API.* `PredictiveStudio.TrainModel` refuses `asOf`, `labelEventDates`, `maxRows` and `primaryKeyField` by
>   name; the legacy `/train` sidecar route and `ISidecarTrainer.train` are removed; `TrainModel` returns no `modelId`
>   when the gate stores `no-signal` (`status: "NoSignal"`). *Regression strategy:* the mapping tests and the M11.4
>   runtime calls; PR 2's G0.8 measures the refusals.
> - *Metric direction.* `MetricDirections.IsErrorMetric` / `MetricDirections.MetricDirectionOf` rank Brier, the deviances, MASE and
>   their legacy spellings lower-is-better (they ranked higher-is-better before, F-TR-6); an unknown metric is not
>   guessed. Experiment leaderboards no longer carry `cvScore` and an experiment without its success metric on the
>   holdout is unscored (`null`, not `0`).
> - *Drivers.* Per-row drivers are centred on the mean encoded training row; a linear model trained before this PR has
>   no stored mean and returns no drivers (never an uncentred one). *Remediation:* retrain.
> - *Compute cost.* `ComputeCost` is `ComputeSeconds × PS_COMPUTE_USD_PER_SECOND`, NULL when the rate is not configured
>   (was written as 0).
> - *Storage.* A new storage provider row `Local File System Storage` is the default snapshot store
>   (`PS_SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_PROVIDER`); multi-host installs point it at a cloud provider.
> - *Gate functions.* The ported contract functions ship only as statics (`GateRules.DecideGate`,
>   `GateRules.GateInputsFromIntervals`, `GateRules.BeatsByMargin`, `GateRules.DecideGuardedGate`,
>   `EvaluationProtocol.ToNonNegative`); the aliases PR 2 removed (`isErrorMetric`, `deriveTrustVerdict`,
>   `trustEvidenceLine`) are not re-added.
>   Free functions this PR changes move to their owner classes with no alias (program D-052): `IsErrorMetric` →
>   `MetricDirections.IsErrorMetric` (`@memberjunction/predictive-studio-core`), `ToBusinessPredictionCard` /
>   `BuildBusinessCatalog` → `BusinessPredictions.*` (`@memberjunction/ng-dashboards`), `TrainModelViaEngine` →
>   `TrainingDelegation.TrainModelViaEngine`, `BuildTrainingDeps` → `TrainingDelegation.BuildTrainingDeps`
>   (`@memberjunction/predictive-studio`); an out-of-repo caller breaks at
>   compile time and takes the qualified name. Deprecated aliases in the files this PR modifies are removed with their
>   callers (program D-053) and listed here before merge.
> - *Existing data is not healed:* models, runs and experiment sessions written before this PR keep their stored values;
>   the honest numbers come from retraining (and, for publication, from PR 4's re-verification).
>
> **Naming (program D-039).** Stored and wire JSON shared with the sidecar and the reference contracts
> (`ValidationResults` envelope, trainer request/result, protocol columns) keeps camelCase, each new member carrying the
> naming gate's reviewed-exception marker; every other new exported shape is PascalCase. Gate rows and checks are
> named by dataset and criterion (`C1 -> S1.1`, `ps-gate-c1-s1-1.checks.ts`), never by plan milestone.
>
> **AI-run verification (ruling S1).** Every guard added here has a recorded mutation check (the "Mutation checks"
> table of each milestone); the plan's reviews were adversarial AI reviews; no step relies on a human reading output.
>
> **Not in this PR.** Model registry columns, the publish-time re-verification and status guard, durable artifacts,
> scoring service and monitoring (PR 4); Feature Pipelines writing effective-dated values and pins, agent budgets
> (PR 5).
